pr.title: Depend on GitHub's gh-stack skill instead of vendoring it
pr.head: 87635c996ef74e9bd35faebffe9f348a6353d377

summary: Projector's implement, fix-pr, and start-fix-loop skills open and maintain stacks: chains of pull requests, each based on the branch below it, that GitHub records as one unit. They drive stacks with gh stack, a GitHub CLI extension, and GitHub publishes a gh-stack skill that teaches an agent its commands.

Until now Projector shipped its own edited copy of that skill under skills/gh-stack/. Every upstream release meant diffing the copy and reapplying the edits by hand, and upstream's v0.2.1 rewrite left the copy a release behind. This pull request deletes the copy and depends on upstream instead.

1. Packaging. Both hosts' Projector marketplaces serve upstream's skill, unmodified and pinned to tag v0.2.1, its commit, and a matching version, as a second plugin named gh-stack. In Claude Code the projector plugin declares it as a dependency; Codex has no dependencies, so there it is a plugin of its own.
  2. Installer. claude plugin update does not install a dependency a plugin newly declares, so install.sh installs or updates gh-stack@projector by name on both hosts. Its default all target also installs the gh stack extension, or upgrades one older than the pin, and status reports the extension against the pin.
  3. Projector's rules. The edits the copy carried become rules in implement's "Stack dependent work" section that win over upstream's skill: split only at the reviewability ceiling, open every layer as a draft, replace the title and body gh stack submit writes, and never merge.
  4. Documentation. docs/plugins.md and the website say where the skill now comes from, and how to install and update it by hand on each host.

cards.title: Terms
cards.html:
• Vendored: a copy of another project's files kept in this repository.
  • Marketplace: the .claude-plugin/marketplace.json catalog Claude Code installs Projector's plugins from.
  • git-subdir source: a marketplace entry that installs one directory of another Git repository at a given ref.
  • Layer: one pull request in a stack.

groups.title: Install upstream's skill as a dependency
groups.kicker: Both marketplaces serve upstream's skill, and Claude Code's projector plugin depends on it
intro: Claude Code and Codex each install plugins from a marketplace file in this repository: .claude-plugin/marketplace.json and .agents/plugins/marketplace.json. Each used to list one plugin, projector, whose skills/ tree included the copied gh-stack skill. Each now lists a second plugin, gh-stack, fetched from the skills directory of github/gh-stack at tag v0.2.1 and naming ./gh-stack as its one skill, a shape both hosts load.

In Claude Code the projector plugin names gh-stack in dependencies. Codex has no plugin dependencies, so its manifest declares none and the installer adds the plugin separately. A newer upstream reaches users only when a Projector change moves the ref, sha, and version in both files, and a packaging test fails when the two entries disagree.

checks.text: In empty configs, a fresh Claude Code install of projector@projector from this head also installs gh-stack@projector at 0.2.1, and claude plugin details lists one skill, gh-stack. In Codex, codex plugin add gh-stack@projector installs a plugin holding gh-stack/SKILL.md. Tag v0.2.1 resolves to the pinned commit.

groups.title: Install the plugin and the extension from the installer
groups.kicker: install.sh adds gh-stack on each host and keeps the gh stack extension at the pin
intro: install.sh is what project upgrade and the one-line installer run. On Claude Code it updates an installed projector with claude plugin update, which moves only that plugin: it neither installs a dependency the new version declares nor moves one already installed. So the installer now installs gh-stack@projector by name when it is missing and updates it when it is present. On Codex it runs codex plugin add gh-stack@projector, which installs or reinstalls it.

The default all target also manages the gh stack GitHub CLI extension. It installs github/gh-stack when gh is present and no extension provides gh stack, upgrades one older than the marketplace's pin, and leaves one from another owner alone. None of these steps fails the install: each failure prints a warning row, because Projector's skills fall back to base branches without the extension.

checks.text: In an empty Claude Code config, I installed projector from the base's marketplace, refreshed the marketplace to this head, and ran the installer's commands in order. claude plugin update projector@projector left gh-stack missing, and the claude plugin install gh-stack@projector --scope user that follows installed it. A second run's update reports it current.

files.note: Adds install_claude_gh_stack, the Codex gh-stack add, install_gh_stack for the extension, and a status row comparing the extension with the pin.

checks.text: Against a marketplace that does not serve gh-stack yet, the install fails with "not found in marketplace", and this function turns that into a warning row, leaving Projector installed.
A real gh extension list prints the command, the repository, and the version separated by tabs, the shape gh_stack_extension parses.

files.note: Fakes gh beside the two hosts, and covers installing and updating gh-stack, a marketplace without it, and each extension case, including status.

groups.title: Keep Projector's stack rules in implement
groups.kicker: The edits the copy carried become rules that win over upstream's skill
intro: The copied skill differed from upstream in four ways that matter to Projector's review loop. Since upstream's skill now ships unmodified, implement's "Stack dependent work" section states those differences as rules that win wherever the two disagree.

• Split only at the reviewability ceiling. Upstream suggests a new layer when a diff grows large or moves to tests; Projector splits only when one review would hold unrelated arguments, and keeps tests and documentation with their code.
  • Draft every layer. --open readies new and existing layers alike, and only a clean review should mark a layer ready.
  • Replace the generated title and body. gh stack submit writes a body with a stack footer and no ## Testing section, and titles a layer of several commits with its branch name.
  • Never merge. Upstream documents gh stack merge; merging stays the user's checkpoint.

files.note: Points at upstream's skill instead of the deleted file, adds the four rules, and cites upstream's "Exit 3 recovery" for rebase conflicts.

checks.text: Upstream's v0.2.1 SKILL.md has the "Exit 3 recovery" list this line cites, describing gh stack rebase --continue and --abort.
Upstream's references/commands.md confirms this: with --auto, a one-commit branch takes its commit's subject and body, and a branch of several commits takes its humanized branch name as the title.

groups.title: Say where the skill comes from
groups.kicker: Plugin documentation and the website describe the dependency
intro: docs/plugins.md explains that both marketplaces serve upstream's skill, that Claude Code installs it with projector while Codex installs it separately, what the installer does about the plugin and the extension, and the commands to install and update both plugins by hand. The website's agents section says the marketplace serves GitHub's gh-stack skill.

checks.text: Anyone who updates only projector@projector by hand, without the installer, still lacks gh-stack. The page tells them to run claude plugin install gh-stack@projector --scope user once, or project upgrade.

files.note: Says Claude Code installs GitHub's gh-stack skill, instead of listing it as one of the plugin's own skills.
